title: Speculative Imbalance Positions by Non-Physical Traders: Impacts on Electricity System Balancing in Great Britain
abstract: arXiv:2610.28075v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The electricity system in Great Britain (GB) allows participants to deliberately produce or consume a different volume to their traded position and has incentivised this practice with a single imbalance price since 2015. In particular, non-physical traders (NPTs) often take an open position to imbalance without any intention to produce or consume power. However, new government proposals could restrict this practice due to concerns over supply-demand balancing feasibility and costs. This article presents the first empirical analysis of speculative imbalance positioning (SIP) by NPTs in the GB electricity system through its effects on imbalance volumes, balancing costs, the imbalance price, and associated settlement costs over the period 2021-2024. Our research uses party-level imbalance data in each settlement period to run counterfactual simulations of the electricity balancing mechanism without the aggregate NPT imbalance. Our results

translated_title: 非实体交易者的投机性不平衡头寸：对英国电力系统平衡的影响
translated_abstract: 英国（GB）电力系统允许参与者故意生产或消费与其交易头寸不同数量的电力，并自2015年起通过单一不平衡价格机制激励这种做法。尤其是非实体交易者（NPTs）经常在不打算生产或消耗任何电力的情况下持有开放的不平衡头寸。然而，出于对供需平衡可行性和成本的担忧，政府的新提案可能会限制这种做法。本文通过考察2021至2024年期间非实体交易者对不平衡电量、平衡成本、不平衡价格及相关结算费用的影响，首次对英国电力系统中非实体交易者的投机性不平衡头寸（SIP）进行了实证分析。我们的研究利用每个结算周期内参与方级别的不平衡数据，在假设不存在非实体交易者总体不平衡的情况下，对电力平衡机制进行了反事实模拟。我们的结果表明……
tldr: 该论文首次实证分析了英国电力市场中非实体交易者的投机性不平衡头寸，通过反事实模拟量化了其对不平衡电量、平衡成本、不平衡价格及结算费用的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first empirical analysis of speculative imbalance positioning by non-physical traders in the GB electricity system, using counterfactual simulations to quantify its impacts on imbalance volumes, balancing costs, imbalance prices, and settlement costs from 2021 to 2024.
